body.zh-HK:
> 面試官問：「一個 reviewer queue 會按嚴重程度同到期時間排工作。個案可以被更新、撤回，或者已經畀另一個 worker 完成。你點樣避免 priority queue 拎到一張已過期嘅工作？」
>
> 答啱一半嘅答案：「我會用 max heap；優先度改咗就直接改 heap 入面嗰個 node。」

Heap 適合由一堆候選工作之中快啲拎出最高優先度，但它唔係個案嘅真實狀態。實際系統入面，一張 case 可能喺排隊後被更正、暫停、交咗人處理，或者已被另一個 worker claim。就算你有 index map 可以改 heap 裏面嘅 node，都未答到並發 worker、crash 後重跑，同埋優先度政策改咗時邊一份資料先算準。

## Heap 只排候選，不是個案真相

將資料分兩層。權威 case record 用 `case_id` 做 key，保留 `version`、state、eligible time、policy input 同最後一次決定。Heap entry 只是一張候選卡：`case_id`、當時的 `version`、rank、排入時間。當 case 的資料或 rank 改變，通常不要嘗試在 heap 內到處找舊 node；寫入新 version，再放一張新卡入 heap。

Worker pop 到一張卡後，先讀權威 record，確認 version 一樣、仍是 eligible、未完成，然後用短 lease 或 compare-and-swap claim 它。任何一項不符，這張卡就是 stale entry，丟掉再 pop 下一張。這種 lazy invalidation 令舊卡可以暫時留在 heap，但不能令舊決定落地。若 stale entry 太多，再在可預期的條件下 rebuild heap；不要把 rebuild 當作每次 pop 的秘密副作用。

Priority 亦要是明文政策，不是一個神秘分數。你可以把 severity、due time、等待時間和必須交人的標記組成排序 key，但要寫清 tie-break、aging 和哪些 case 永遠不可自動處理。否則最高優先度的 case 不斷湧入，低風險但仍要處理的工作可以永遠餓死。

## 排隊便條不是個案紀錄

想像郵局有一大疊寫住「最急」的便條。Heap 幫你由頂拎一張最快，但真正的包裹狀態喺登記簿：可能已派送、地址已改，或者有人叫停。拎到便條後先核對登記簿，先可以交包裹；唔可以因為便條排第一就當它仍然有效。

## 面試時要講到的決定

一個完整答案可以是：「我用 heap 排候選，而 case table 才是 state 的 source of truth。每張 entry 帶 case ID 同 version；worker pop 後重新核對 eligibility，再以 lease 或原子 claim 防止雙重處理。更新會產生新 entry，舊 entry 被 lazy discard；我會量度 stale-pop rate、最舊 eligible case 的等待時間、不同 severity 的等待分布和重複 claim。」

這樣講出的是資料結構同工作政策的分工。AI Engineer 不是只要說 `O(log n)`；還要知道這個排序會影響誰先被 reviewer 看見、哪種錯誤會被延後，以及事故後怎樣重建可核對的 queue。

## 別只講時間複雜度

「Heap 的 push 和 pop 很快」是對的，但太薄。追問會包括：case priority 降低時怎麼辦？兩張同分的 case 要怎樣穩定排序？worker 在 lease 後 crash 了怎麼辦？一個 case 由權限規則變成 blocked 時，舊 entry 為何不會穿過？

用 fixed cases 證明答案：已完成 case 的舊 entry、priority 被降低的 case、同時 claim、極長等待 case、policy version 改變、以及 heap rebuild 前後的輸出。每個 case 都要寫 expected route，不要只貼一張 queue 截圖。

## 可以留下的工程證據

- `case-state.schema.json`：state、version、eligible time 和 terminal state。
- `priority-policy.md`：排序 key、tie-break、aging、blocked case 和誰批准改 policy。
- `queue-entry.ts`：heap entry 與權威 record 的分別。
- `stale-entry.test.ts`：更新、撤回、雙重 claim、lease expiry 和 rebuild fixture。
- `queue-report.md`：stale-pop rate、最舊 eligible item、重複 claim 和不能自動處理的 handoff。

## 延伸閱讀

[Queue 要有 dead-letter path](/zh-HK/interview-lab/a-queue-needs-a-dead-letter-path)、[Retry 成功，點解 workflow 仍然可以出事？](/zh-HK/interview-lab/a-retry-is-not-a-recovery-plan)，以及 [Coding 同 data structures 題怎樣講到可營運](/zh-HK/interview-lab/coding-and-data-structures)。

## 範圍說明

這是 AI.DOG 的單題練習。review queue、case、priority、worker、指標和 artefact 都是 synthetic 教學材料；它不代表任何機構的個案分流政策、服務容量或真實面試流程。

> 面试官问：“一个 reviewer queue 会按严重程度和到期时间排序工作。个案可能被更新、撤回，或已被另一个 worker 完成。你怎样避免 priority queue 取到一份过期工作？”
>
> 答对一半的答案：“我会用 max heap；优先度变了就直接改 heap 里的 node。”

Heap 适合从一堆候选工作中快速取出最高优先度，但它不是个案的真实状态。实际系统里，一个 case 可能在排队后被更正、暂停、交给人处理，或已被另一个 worker claim。即使有 index map 可以修改 heap 里的 node，仍没有回答并发 worker、crash 后重跑，以及优先度政策改变时哪一份数据才算准。

## Heap 只排候选，不是个案真相

把数据分成两层。权威 case record 用 `case_id` 做 key，保留 `version`、state、eligible time、policy input 和最后一次决策。Heap entry 只是一张候选卡：`case_id`、当时的 `version`、rank 与排入时间。当 case 数据或 rank 改变，通常不必在 heap 内四处寻找旧 node；写入新 version，再放一张新卡进 heap。

Worker pop 到一张卡后，先读权威 record，确认 version 相同、仍可处理、尚未完成，再以短 lease 或 compare-and-swap claim 它。任何一项不符，这张卡就是 stale entry，丢掉后再 pop 下一张。这种 lazy invalidation 让旧卡暂时留在 heap，却不能让旧决策落地。若 stale entry 太多，再在明确条件下 rebuild heap；不要把 rebuild 当成每次 pop 的隐藏副作用。

Priority 也要是明文政策，不是一个神秘分数。你可以把 severity、due time、等待时间与必须交人的标记组成排序 key，但要写清 tie-break、aging，以及哪些 case 永远不可自动处理。否则高优先度 case 不断涌入时，低风险但仍要处理的工作可能永远得不到处理。

## 排队便条不是个案记录

想象邮局有一大叠写着“最急”的便条。Heap 帮你最快从顶端取一张，但真正的包裹状态在登记簿：可能已派送、地址已改，或有人叫停。拿到便条后先核对登记簿，才可以交包裹；不能因为便条排第一就当它仍然有效。

## 面试时要讲到的决策

一个完整答案可以是：“我用 heap 排候选，而 case table 才是 state 的 source of truth。每张 entry 带 case ID 与 version；worker pop 后重新核对 eligibility，再用 lease 或原子 claim 防止双重处理。更新会产生新 entry，旧 entry 被 lazy discard；我会量测 stale-pop rate、最旧 eligible case 的等待时间、不同 severity 的等待分布与重复 claim。”

这说明数据结构与工作政策的分工。AI Engineer 不只要说 `O(log n)`；还要知道排序会影响谁先被 reviewer 看见、哪种错误会被延后，以及事故后怎样重建可核对的 queue。

## 别只讲时间复杂度

“Heap 的 push 与 pop 很快”是对的，但太薄。追问会包括：case priority 降低时怎么办？两张同分 case 如何稳定排序？worker 在 lease 后 crash 怎么办？一个 case 因权限规则变成 blocked 时，旧 entry 为什么不会穿过？

用 fixed cases 证明答案：已完成 case 的旧 entry、priority 被降低的 case、同时 claim、极长等待 case、policy version 改变，以及 heap rebuild 前后的输出。每个 case 都要写 expected route，不要只贴一张 queue 截图。

## 可以留下的工程证据

- `case-state.schema.json`：state、version、eligible time 与 terminal state。
- `priority-policy.md`：排序 key、tie-break、aging、blocked case 与谁批准改 policy。
- `queue-entry.ts`：heap entry 与权威 record 的差异。
- `stale-entry.test.ts`：更新、撤回、双重 claim、lease expiry 与 rebuild fixture。
- `queue-report.md`：stale-pop rate、最旧 eligible item、重复 claim 与不能自动处理的 handoff。

## 范围说明

这是 AI.DOG 的单题练习。review queue、case、priority、worker、指标与 artefact 都是 synthetic 教学材料；不代表任何机构的个案分流政策、服务容量或真实面试流程。
body.en:
> Interviewer asks: “A reviewer queue orders work by severity and due time. A case may be changed, withdrawn, or completed by another worker. How do you stop the priority queue from processing an old entry?”
>
> Half-right answer: “I would use a max heap and update the heap node when the priority changes.”

A heap quickly selects the highest-ranked candidate, but it is not the case's true state. In a real system, a case may be corrected, paused, handed to a person, or claimed by another worker after it enters the queue. Even an index map that supports heap-node updates does not settle concurrent workers, crash recovery, or which version of the priority policy is authoritative.

## A heap orders candidates, not the source of truth

Keep two layers. The authoritative case record is keyed by `case_id` and carries its `version`, state, eligible time, policy inputs, and latest decision. A heap entry is only a candidate card: `case_id`, the version seen at enqueue time, rank, and enqueue time. When the case or its rank changes, do not rely on finding every old node inside the heap. Write a new version and enqueue a new card.

After a worker pops a card, it reads the authoritative record, checks that the version still matches, that the case is eligible and unfinished, then claims it with a short lease or compare-and-swap. If any check fails, the card is stale: discard it and pop again. This lazy invalidation lets old cards remain temporarily in the heap without letting an old decision take effect. If stale cards become too common, rebuild the heap under an explicit condition; do not make rebuilding a hidden side effect of every pop.

Priority must also be a stated policy, not a mysterious number. Severity, due time, waiting time, and a mandatory-handoff marker may form a rank key, but document tie-breaking, aging, and cases that must never be automated. Otherwise an endless stream of urgent work can starve lower-risk work that still deserves review.

## A queue slip is not the case record

Imagine a post office with a tall stack of notes marked “most urgent.” The heap helps you take the top note quickly. The actual parcel status lives in the registry: it may already be delivered, have a new address, or be stopped by a supervisor. Check the registry after taking the note and before moving the parcel. Its position in the stack is not proof that it is still valid.

## The decision an interviewer is listening for

A useful answer is: “I use a heap to order candidates, while the case table remains the source of truth. Each entry carries a case ID and version. After pop, a worker checks eligibility again and uses a lease or atomic claim to prevent double processing. Updates create a new entry; stale ones are discarded lazily. I would measure stale-pop rate, age of the oldest eligible case, waiting-time distribution by severity, and duplicate claims.”

That explains how the data structure and the work policy divide responsibility. An AI Engineer is not finished after saying `O(log n)`: the order changes which person sees a case first, which errors wait longer, and how an operator can rebuild a queue after an incident.

## Where an answer goes thin

“Heap push and pop are fast” is true but incomplete. Expect questions such as: What happens when a priority falls? How do equal ranks stay stable? What happens if a worker crashes after leasing a case? Why cannot an old entry pass through after a permission rule blocks the case?

Prove the design with fixed cases: an old entry for a completed case, a lowered priority, concurrent claims, a long-waiting case, a policy-version change, and the output before and after a heap rebuild. Give every case an expected route; do not rely on a queue screenshot.

## Engineering artefacts to leave behind

- `case-state.schema.json`: state, version, eligible time, and terminal states.
- `priority-policy.md`: rank key, tie-breaking, aging, blocked cases, and who may change the policy.
- `queue-entry.ts`: the distinction between a heap entry and the authoritative record.
- `stale-entry.test.ts`: update, withdrawal, duplicate-claim, lease-expiry, and rebuild fixtures.
- `queue-report.md`: stale-pop rate, oldest eligible item, duplicate claims, and handoffs that cannot be automated.

## Further reading

[A queue needs a dead-letter path](/en/interview-lab/a-queue-needs-a-dead-letter-path), [a retry is not a recovery plan](/en/interview-lab/a-retry-is-not-a-recovery-plan), and [connecting coding and data structures to an operable system](/en/interview-lab/coding-and-data-structures).

## Scope note

This is an AI.DOG single-question exercise. The review queue, cases, priorities, workers, measures, and artefacts are synthetic teaching material; they do not describe any organisation's triage policy, service capacity, or interview process.
